drivers: five small features with strong consistency between tickets, replies and status
no independent scaling or release need
no packages may be installed in this run, so one stdlib Python process is the simplest buildable shape

alternatives.reason: a separate FAQ service adds network calls and deployables for one pure function
suggestions are computed synchronously from the ticket text; nothing is asynchronous
there is no existing system that must stay separate; Faqbot is a 4-line module

style.reason: The simplest design that meets every driver

stack.backend: Python 3.8+ standard library: wsgiref HTTP server, sqlite3
stack.frontend: server-rendered HTML forms from the same process, no JavaScript build
stack.hosting: not decided; runs locally (no deployment in this run)

reasons.backend: D01: B is the user's own Python; A's JavaScript may not be reused; no installs are approved, and stdlib Python needs none
reasons.frontend: D02: three screens of forms; no client framework needed
reasons.database: D03: one small team, low volume; SQLite gives check constraints and foreign keys with no server
reasons.hosting: D04: deployment is out of scope (plan mode; never automatic)

modules.name: config
modules.responsibility: read every setting from environment variables with development defaults

modules.name: accounts
modules.responsibility: agent accounts, password sign-in, server-side sessions, the may-this-agent-do-this check

modules.name: faq
modules.responsibility: FAQ entries and the improved suggestion matcher (from B)

modules.name: tickets
modules.responsibility: ticket lifecycle, replies and closing (from A); asks faq for suggestions on a ticket's subject and description

modules.name: web
modules.responsibility: HTTP routing, JSON API, HTML pages, one error format

entities.name: Agent
entities.notes: platform piece: no source has users; needed to record who replied

entities.name: Ticket
entities.notes: status check constraint open|pending|closed; index on status and created_at

entities.name: Message
entities.notes: A's embedded Ticket.messages list becomes rows with ticket_id; index on (ticket_id, created_at)

auth.method: email and password (PBKDF2-SHA256 via hashlib, per-agent salt)
auth.session: random token in an http-only, SameSite=Lax cookie (Secure outside development); only its SHA-256 is stored; expires after SESSION_TTL_MINUTES

navigation.screen: Ticket with suggested answers, thread, reply and close

design_system.tokens: one CSS file: colour roles (surface, text, muted, accent, danger), 4-step type scale, 4px spacing grid, 6px radius

configuration.HELPDESK_ENV: development or production (Secure cookies in production)

slices.name: Core loop: create a ticket and see suggested FAQ answers
Work the ticket: reply and close

decisions.reason: B is the user's own Python; A's code cannot be reused; no installs approved

decisions.decision: Server-rendered HTML plus a JSON API under /api/v1
decisions.reason: few screens; one API for tests and future clients

decisions.decision: SQLite with foreign keys on and check constraints
decisions.reason: small scale, enforce A's status rule in the database
plan mode; deployment is never automatic

decisions.decision: Modular monolith with modules config, accounts, faq, tickets, web
Agents sign in with email and password; accounts created by an admin command, no public sign-up; one role 'agent'
decisions.reason: neither source has users; replies need a real author; minimum identity the kept features need

decisions.decision: Agents may set a ticket to open or pending (POST /status); closing stays a separate action with A's rule
decisions.reason: A defines 'pending' and refuses to close it, but no code moves a ticket into pending; without a transition the rule cannot be reached. Open question for the user

decisions.decision: Suggestions match subject and description only; punctuation stripped, stop words ignored, ranked by shared words, at most 3
decisions.reason: compatibility decision application:workflow:suggestion-input and the M05 improvement

decisions.decision: No email delivery, no payments, and none of A's environment variables are carried over
decisions.reason: email is a documented claim contradicted by A's code; the payment key has no feature behind it; A's .env holds a live-looking secret that must never be copied
one error shape and one pagination style for the whole API
